jobs.title: Project Coordinator
jobs.description:
About Us

Channing House is a leading not-for-profit Life Plan Community in Palo Alto, founded in 1960. We believe that older adults thrive in a vibrant setting that supports active, engaged and healthy living. We provide a sustainable, innovative community that promotes this lifestyle, while embracing respect and dignity for all who live and work here. Our team of 200 staff members, from Front-Line to Leadership, drive the mission of Channing House, providing services to the 265 highly engaged residents who call Channing House their home.

Position Summary

The Project Coordinator will play a key role in supporting capital improvement, renovations, construction, and operational initiatives under the directions of the Director of Facilities & Operations. Major initiatives include the development and opening of the new Arris building, campus renovations and improvements, resident move-ins and transitions, and the expansion of Memory Care services.

This position coordinates multiple concurrent projects, facilitates communication among stakeholders, maintains project documentation, tracks budget and milestones, and supports the timely completion of project deliverables.

The Project Coordinator is highly organized, detail-oriented, and comfortable coordinating work across departments and with residents, committees, contractors, consultants, vendors, and other external partners. Experience with facility renovations, design and construction processes, project coordination, and healthcare or senior living environments is strongly preferred.

The Project Coordinator exemplifies our Core Values: Do the right thing; Be a team player; Focus on quality; Adapt to change Together with the entire team at Channing House, this role contributes to promoting a healthy and vibrant home for our residents.

Key Responsibilities

This position will be responsible for, but not limited to the following essential duties and responsibilities:

Project Coordination and Capital Improvements – 75%

Support the Director of Facilities & Operations with the planning, coordination, implementation, and closeout of capital improvement, renovation, facilities, and operational projects.
Coordinate multiple projects that vary in size, complexity, and duration. Current and anticipated projects include, but not limited to:
Design, permitting, construction, opening, and ongoing development of the new Arris building
Physical environment changes supporting the Memory Care Program
Tower renovations and improvements
Lobby renovation
Dining room renovation
11th floor improvements
Outdoor space enhancements
Skilled Nursing and Wellness Wing Refresh
Future property development, renovations, and building improvements
Support future renovations, building improvements, operational initiatives, and other projects assigned by the Director of Facilities & Operations.
Develop and maintain detailed project plans, schedules, timelines, budgets, action-items lists, and status reports.
Monitor project milestones, deadlines, and deliverables and proactively identify potential delays, risks, operational impacts, and resource constraints.
Track project progress against established plans and follow up with responsible parties to support the timely completion of deliverables.
Escalate delays, risks, budget concerns, competing priorities, and unresolved issues to the Director of Facilities & Operations as appropriate.
Coordinate project meetings, prepare agendas and supporting materials, document decisions, maintain meeting notes, and track action items through completion.
Coordinate activities across departments and help ensure project responsivities, deadlines, dependencies, and operational impacts are clearly communicated.
Serve as a central point of contact for assigned projects and ensure questions, concerns, and decisions are routed to the appropriate individuals.
Coordinate with architects, engineers, contractors, consultants, vendors, inspectors, regulatory agencies, and other project partners.
Coordinate vendor and contractor meetings, schedules, site access, required documentation, and communication with affected departments.
Support project design, permitting, construction, inspections, commissioning, punch-list completion, and closeout activities.
Track proposals, contracts, purchase orders, project expenses, budgets, change orders, invoices, and supporting documentation.
Review project documentation for completeness and route materials for appropriate review and approval.
Monitor project costs against approved budgets and promptly identify potential discrepancies or cost concerns.
Maintain organized, accurate, and current project records, including applicable approvals, permits, warranties, operating manuals, inspection records, and closeout documents.
Coordinate communications regarding project schedules, closures, service interruptions, construction impacts, and changes affecting residents, employees, visitors, and other stakeholders.
Help ensure projects are coordinated in a manner that supports resident safety and minimizes disruption to residents, employees, and daily operations.
Identify and document opportunities to improve project coordination, communication, operational processes, and project outcomes.

Operational and Departmental Support – 25%

Coordinate operational projects and initiatives under the direction of the Director of Facilities & Operations.
Assist department leaders with developing project plans, coordinating resources, tracking deliverables, and resolving project-related issues.
Support operational readiness, resident move-ins, and transition activities associated with the new Arris building.
Serve as a central point of contact for Arris move-in logistics, operational coordination, issue tracking, and follow-up.
Identify, document, and coordinate the timely resolution of construction, post-move-in, and operational concerns associated with Arris.
Collaborate with the Resident Transition Committee and department leaders to support the integration of Arris residents into the Channing House community.
Coordinate logistics for resident moves, departmental transitions, space changes, service implementations, equipment installations, and other operational initiatives.
Support the implementation of new systems, equipment, programs, procedures, and vendor services.
Assist with collecting information, preparing reports, and tracking performance measures to evaluate project and operational outcomes.
Provide timely and accurate project updates, summaries, presentations, correspondence, and other materials as needed.
Maintain effective working relationships with residents, employees, department leaders, committees, vendors, contractors, consultants, and external partners.
Maintain confidentiality and exercise sound judgment when handling sensitive projects, financial, resident, employee, or organizational information.
Perform other duties and project coordination responsibilities as assigned.

Upholding Company Standards

Consistent commitment to:

Establish and maintain effective team relationships with fellow staff; apply effective communication and listening skills
Demonstrate professionalism in all interactions with all residents, colleagues, clients, vendors, and members of the public
Provide a supportive and caring environment to meet the needs of residents as individuals and as members of a shared community
Adhere to all company policies, procedures, safety, and compliance practices, and business ethics codes

Job Requirements / Qualifications

To perform this job successfully, a person must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability required.

Professional Experience

At least three years of experience in project coordination, operations, facilities, constructions administration, executive administration, healthcare, senior living, or related field.
Strong organizational, planning, time management, and follow-through skills.
Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.
Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously and adapt to changing priorities, deadlines, and operational needs.
Strong attention to detail and ability to maintain accurate and organized project records.
Ability to work collaboratively across departments and with residents, committees, contractors, consultants, vendors, and other external partners.
Preferred:
Experience in senior living, healthcare, hospitality, residential community, construction, or facilities environments.
Understanding of design, permitting, renovation, construction, or facility improvement processes.
Experience coordinating contractors, consultants, architects, engineers, or vendors.
Familiarity with project management principles, methodologies and best practices.
Familiarity with regulatory requirements applicable to California healthcare, assisted living, memory care, or continuing care retirement communities.

Educational/Position Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in project management, construction management, facilities management, business administration, or a related field preferred.
An equivalent combination of education, training, and relevant experience will be considered.

Computer/Software/Technical Applications

Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite.
Experience using project management, scheduling, document-management, or project-tracking tools preferred.
Ability to learn and effectively use organization-specific software and systems.

Languages

Ability to speak, read, write, and comprehend English the primary language used in the workplace; ability to speak and/or comprehend other languages utilized by staff is a plus.

Required Licenses/ Certifications/ Background

Must possess a current, valid California-issued driver's license and maintain an acceptable driving record.

Travel Required

Less than 10%

Skills

Speaking — Talking to others to convey information effectively.
Active Listening — Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.
Reading Comprehension — Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work related documents.
Critical Thinking — Use logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions or approaches to problems.
Writing — Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.
Service Orientation — Actively looking for ways to help people.
Customer Service — Manages difficult or emotional situations involving residents, resident families, and/or staff; responds promptly to needs of residents, resident families, and/or staff; responds to requests for service and assistance.
Social Perceptiveness — Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.
Time Management — Managing one's own time and the time of others.
Professionalism — Presents self in a highly professional manner to others and communicate with co-workers and other departments with professionalism and respect. Maintains a professional relationship with all coworkers, vendor representatives, supervisors, managers, residents, and resident families.
Quality Management — Looks for ways to improve and promote quality.
Safety and Security — Observes safety and security requirements, reports potentially unsafe conditions, and supports contractor, vendor, and project compliance with established procedures.
Active Learning — Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.
Cultural Awareness - Demonstrates knowledge of EEO policy; shows respect and sensitivity for cultural differences; promotes a harassment-free environment.
Judgment and Decision Making — Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one

jobs.title: Environmental Scientist
jobs.description:
About the Company

We're working with a well-established environmental consulting firm seeking an Environmental Scientist with 2+ years of experience supporting environmental field investigations and regulatory compliance projects throughout New Jersey. This is an excellent opportunity for someone looking to build their career with a company that offers a diverse project workload, professional development, and long-term growth.

About the Role

As an Environmental Scientist
, you will be responsible for conducting environmental field investigations and site assessments, performing soil, groundwater, sediment, and surface water sampling, and supporting remediation projects and environmental compliance activities.

Responsibilities

Conduct environmental field investigations and site assessments.
Perform soil, groundwater, sediment, and surface water sampling.
Support remediation projects and environmental compliance activities.
Document field observations and maintain accurate field records.
Prepare technical reports and assist with NJDEP regulatory submissions.
Coordinate with project managers and multidisciplinary project teams.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Geology, Environmental Engineering, or a related field.
2+ years of environmental consulting experience.
Experience performing NJDEP-regulated field work.
Familiarity with Phase I/II Environmental Site Assessments, remedial investigations, and site remediation projects is preferred.
Working knowledge of NJDEP regulations and guidance.
Strong technical writing and communication skills.
Valid driver's license with the ability to travel to project sites throughout New Jersey.

Required Skills

Strong technical writing and communication skills.
Working knowledge of NJDEP regulations and guidance.

Preferred Skills

Familiarity with Phase I/II Environmental Site Assessments, remedial investigations, and site remediation projects.

jobs.title: Senior Project Coordinator
jobs.description:
Position Summary

Perform a wide variety of professional project management duties for renovation and new development projects including professional and technical architectural or landscape architectural services and activities, construction management, capital project fiscal planning, project planning, design, plan check, inspection, project budgets and scheduling; supervise the work of staff and consultants responsible for performing a wide variety of multiple technical and professional projects in support of assigned projects; coordinate assigned activities with other divisions, departments and outside agencies.

Job descriptions are intended to present a general list of tasks/duties performed by employees within this job classification. Job Descriptions are not intended to reflect all duties performed within the job.

Essential And Supplemental Functions

SSENTIAL FUNCTIONS: Essential functions may include, but are not limited to the functions listed below. Must be able to perform the essential functions of the job with or without a reasonable accommodation.

Assume management and supervisory responsibility for professional and technical architectural or landscape architectural services and activities, construction management, capital project fiscal planning, project planning, design, plan check, inspection, project budgets and scheduling for multiple capital projects.
Plan, direct, coordinate, assign, review and evaluate the work activities, products, methods and procedures of staff and consultants responsible for performing a wide variety of multiple professional and technical renovation and new development of capital projects.
Recommend design consultants, negotiate contract agreements, review and approve design and construction documents and pay requests for consultants and contractors.
Represent the Division/Department/City at public meetings and City Council before boards and commissions and to other divisions, departments and agencies for assigned projects.
Participate in identifying and resolving conflict and project related problems with solutions that result in resource savings (time, money, staff).
Serve as a liaison for the Division/Department/City with other City departments, divisions, the public and outside agencies; coordinate, negotiate, resolve sensitive and controversial issues.
Develop project status reports and construction schedules; estimate project construction costs and develop budget sheets.
Respond and resolve difficult and sensitive citizen inquires and complaints related to assigned projects.
Serve as project manager for assigned capital projects.
Participate in inspection services for assigned capital (CIP) projects.
Review and make recommendations on development plans, construction plans or architectural designs and specifications.

SUPPLEMENTAL FUNCTIONS:

May act in the absence of the Division Manager.
Attend and participate in professional training, group meetings, seminars and activities; stay abreast of new trends and innovations in the field of Landscape or related field.
Perform other related duties and responsibilities as assigned.

Minimum Education, Experience And Additional Requirements

Education and experience directly related to the minimum requirements below may be interchangeable on a year for year basis.

Bachelor's degree in business administration, construction management, architectural design, or landscape architecture; and

Five (5) years of experience in any combination of the following areas:

managerial construction
professional architectural
landscape architectural
capital project management

To include
two (2) years of supervisory experience.

Additional Requirements

Possession of a valid New Mexico Driver's License, or the ability to obtain by date of hire.

Possession of a City Operator's Permit (COP) within 6 months from date of hire.

Possession of Professional Landscape Architect (PLA) licensure preferred.

Working Conditions

Environmental

Office, field and construction environment; exposure to computer screens; occasional exposure to noise, dust, grease, smoke, fumes, gases, inclement weather conditions and work around heavy construction equipment.

Physical

Essential and supplemental functions may require maintaining physical condition necessary for walking, standing or sitting for prolonged periods of time.

jobs.title: Quality Control Field Technician
jobs.description:
Discover a more connected career

At Ansco & Associates, LLC, as a Quality Control Field Technician, you’ll ensure that construction or installation work meets specified standards by performing inspections, conducting tests, and monitoring compliance throughout projects. You’ll address issues, document findings, and collaborate with teams to implement improvements and maintain high-quality outcomes

Connecting You To Great Benefits

Weekly Paychecks
Paid Time Off, Parental Leave, and Holidays
Insurance (including medical, prescription drug, dental, vision, disability, life insurance)
401(k) w/ Company Match
Stock Purchase Plan
Education Reimbursement
Legal Insurance
Discounts on gym memberships, pet insurance, and much more!

What You’ll Do

Conduct quality inspections during the installation process to ensure work meets plans and specifications
Perform final inspections as requested by customers to ensure compliance with construction standards
Identify issues and report them to relevant team members for resolution
Record and follow up on non-compliance issues until they are resolved
Ensure all required testing is completed as specified and document the results
Follow installation milestones and support project activities as directed by management
Work overtime, travel, and handle on-call or after-hours responsibilities as needed, and perform duties in all weather conditions
Other duties as assigned

What You’ll Need

To be 18 years of age or older
Authorization to work in the United States for this company
Valid State driver's license (cannot be Provisional), including an acceptable driving record
One year of relevant work experience

Additional Qualifications

Quality control experience preferred
Associates Degree in an industry related field or equivalent work experience
Knowledge and understanding of the telecommunication construction industry standard practices
Knowledge of Customer Installation Standards and Documentation

Physical Abilities & Exposures

Routinely: work alone in remote locations, operate vehicle, squeeze, bend, stoop, stand, walking, climb stairs, use keyboard and mouse
Occasionally: work at heights, use ladder, life greater than 55 pounds

Why grow your career with us

Your career here is more than just a job — it's your pathway to opportunity. Our hands-on training, supportive environment, and responsive leadership connect you to work with purpose. Our commitment to you extends beyond professional development to a safety-first culture that ensures you can do what you do best, with peace of mind.

Building stronger solutions together

Our company is an equal-opportunity employer — we are committed to providing a work environment where everyone can thrive, grow, and feel connected.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status.

jobs.description:

• Transform complex data into actionable insights through advanced visualization techniques.

jobs.title: Program Coordinator
jobs.description:
Job Description

The Program Coordinator within the Office of Student Affairs plays a critical role in ensuring the efficient and effective functioning of daily business operations. This position serves as the linchpin for coordinating a range of administrative activities, procurement processes, event planning, budget oversight, and database management. With a focus on maintaining seamless operations, the Program Coordinator collaborates closely with the Associate Dean of Student Affairs, the Director of Student Affairs , the Assistant Director of Student Financial Assistance, and the Assistant Director of Leadership Development and Wellness. This position is essential to the overall success of the department and the Joan C. Edwards School of Medicine. Job responsibilities: Manage the daily business operations for the Office of Student Affairs and serve as the point of contact for visitors Provides backup and support for the Office of Student Affairs Facilitate the creation, review, and processing of purchase orders and PARs Manage the purchasing, requisition, and Marketplace processes for the Office of Student Affairs Manage Student and Academic Affairs budgets and track expenditures Maintain up-to-date student information databases Oversee student lounges and address concerns as they arise Oversee and coordinate and oversee logistics, planning, and execution of student School of Medicine events Oversee the Astra room reservation system Manage, compile, and analyze on post-event surveys Development, distribution, and conducting initial analysis of online surveys Analyze and report on student outcome measures Responsible for coordinating travel arrangements for students, faculty, and staff Manage the distribution of parking permits and other needed student items Administer the organization, communication and collection of funds for student group packages for medical board exam prep Administrative support contact for student organizations Performs all other duties as assigned

jobs.title: Project Coordinator
jobs.description:
Position: PROJECT ENGINEERING MANAGER

About the Opportunity

Our client is seeking an experienced Project Engineering Manager to lead complex capital and engineering projects within a food manufacturing environment. This leadership role oversees engineering design, project execution, contractors, budgets, and cross-functional collaboration while driving safe, efficient project delivery.
Key Responsibilities

• Lead large-scale engineering and capital projects from concept through completion
• Develop engineering designs, specifications, budgets, and cost estimates
• Conduct feasibility studies and engineering reviews
• Coordinate plant personnel, contractors, vendors, and consultants
• Manage schedules, contracts, bid packages, and project documentation
• Review field work, validate installations, and prepare as-built drawings
• Monitor budgets, project status, and compliance with engineering standards
Qualifications

• Bachelor's Degree in Engineering or related field
• 5+ years of engineering experience and 2+ years of leadership experience
• Strong project management and contract administration skills
• AutoCAD and Microsoft Office proficiency
• Knowledge of construction scheduling and engineering codes
• Multi-million-dollar project experience preferred
• Food processing or meat industry experience is an asset
• Ability to travel up to 50%
Why Join?

Competitive salary of $125,000–$155,000 plus bonus with the opportunity to lead high-impact engineering projects, mentor engineering teams, and influence strategic capital investments within a growing manufacturing organization.

Skills

Speaking — Talking to others to convey information effectively.
Active Listening — Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.
Reading Comprehension — Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work related documents.
Critical Thinking — Use logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions or approaches to problems.
Writing — Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.
Service Orientation — Actively looking for ways to help people.
Customer Service — Manages difficult or emotional situations involving residents, resident families, and/or staff; responds promptly to needs of residents, resident families, and/or staff; responds to requests for service and assistance.
Social Perceptiveness — Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.
Time Management — Managing one's own time and the time of others.
Professionalism — Presents self in a highly professional manner to others and communicate with co-workers and other departments with professionalism and respect. Maintains a professional relationship with all coworkers, vendor representatives, supervisors, managers, residents, and resident families.
Quality Management — Looks for ways to improve and promote quality.
Safety and Security — Observes safety and security requirements, reports potentially unsafe conditions, and supports contractor, vendor, and project compliance with established procedures.
Active Learning — Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.
Cultural Awareness - Demonstrates knowledge of EEO policy; shows respect and sensitivity for cultural differences; promotes a harassment-free environment.
Judgment and Decision Making — Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one
